sections.h2: Who values, bills and collects in Logan County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
Logan County splits property tax among three desks. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) appraises, the Sheriff takes payment on the current bill, and the County Clerk picks up whatever is still open after April 15.

The Sheriff's Office sits at 100 North Owen Street in Russellville and answers at 270-726-2244 on weekdays between 8 am and 4 pm. A link on the county's Sheriff page leads to online payment. The PVA uses PO Box 307, Russellville, KY 42276, and its number is 270-726-8334. Its published duties state that it neither sets rates nor collects tax. The Clerk's Office at 229 West 3rd Street keeps weekday hours until 4:30 with a phone line at 270-726-6061.

Rates come from the elected bodies that levy them: fiscal court, city councils, school boards, and districts like the extension office, library and health department. Once those rates are reported to the clerk, the bills go to print.

sections.h2: What sets Logan County apart as a place to sell a house?
sections.html:
Logan County is farm country with factories, lying against the Tennessee border. It has four cities: Russellville, Adairville, Auburn and Lewisburg. The county covers 557 square miles, 552 of them land, on the southwest side of the Pennyroyal Plateau, and it was carved out of Lincoln County on September 1, 1792. Dark fired tobacco built much of its early money.

Russellville is the seat, home to 7,164 people in 2020, and U.S. 68, 79 and 431 all pass through. The closest limited-access road, the Natcher Parkway (I-165), is about 24 miles to the northeast. Local plants make goods ranging from pet food to plastics, and Logan Aluminum, the biggest employer, lists more than 1,300 workers. Two school systems divide the county: Russellville Independent Schools, with R. E. Stevenson Elementary, Russellville Middle and Russellville High, and Logan County Schools, whose high school bears the county name.

In the 2020 count the county held 12,461 housing units, and roughly seven in ten occupied homes belonged to the people living in them.

sections.h2: How does a Logan County tax bill get its number?
sections.html:
Two inputs produce the bill: an assessed value from the PVA and a combined rate from each district that covers the parcel. Kentucky values real estate at what it would sell for in a voluntary sale on January 1, and farm ground can be valued by its agricultural use.

The PVA calls its online roll a working file, because appeals and assessments keep changing it. The value on that roll comes before exemptions, so subtract any exemption to find the taxable amount. As a rough illustration, a house at the county's $164,900 midpoint with the $49,100 senior exemption would be taxed on $115,800. Rates vary by city versus rural address, so ask the County Clerk for the exact set that applies to you.

One quirk helps buyers and sellers. If a property was bought last year, the price in the deed may stand as the listed value for the next assessment, unless the property changed. The number on a recorded deed can follow the house into future bills.

sections.h2: When does Logan County property tax come due?
sections.html:
The Sheriff mails bills around the first of October, and the state schedule then moves through stages with the amount owed rising as the calendar advances.

  • Oct 1 through Nov 1: face amount minus 2 percent, paid to the Sheriff.
  • Nov 2 through Dec 31: face amount, Sheriff.
  • All of January: face plus 5 percent, Sheriff.
  • Feb 1 through Apr 15: face plus 21 percent, Sheriff.
  • After Apr 15: certificate of delinquency, County Clerk.

A bill that has not turned up by mid-October is worth a call to 270-726-2244. Once the clerk holds it, the bill carries a recorded lien and grows by interest each month plus clerk and county attorney fees. The county attorney's first warning letter goes out by May 15, and an installment plan is still possible at that point.

sections.h2: What steps lead to a lower Logan County assessment?
sections.html:
Meet with the PVA first. Only owners who have held that conference may take a dispute to the clerk.

  • The roll is open to view for thirteen days beginning in early May, including Saturdays.
  • File the appeal at the clerk's office no later than the next workday after that window closes.
  • A panel of local board members hears the case between 25 and 35 days later, and the clerk sets the date.

Come with facts. Without them the panel must deny the appeal. Photos, a recent appraisal, insurance policies, construction costs, and listings or sale contracts all count as proof. Anyone paid to speak for you must be a recognized professional, such as an attorney, accountant, appraiser or licensed broker, and must hold your written authorization. Written findings explain any change, and if you stay unhappy, the state tax appeals board is next. Skipping the local panel ends that route.

sections.h2: Is there relief for Logan County homeowners?
sections.html:
The homestead exemption is the main one. Seniors, and owners classed as totally disabled, take $49,100 off the home's assessed value for 2025 and 2026.

Applications go to the Logan PVA at PO Box 307 in Russellville. Disability filers generally reapply every year, with exceptions for service-connected veteran disability and for rulings of total, permanent disability by the federal or state retirement programs. The PVA also lists exemptions for certain religious, educational and government property.

Landowners with working acreage should raise agricultural valuation with the PVA, since the state allows farm ground to be valued by use.

sections.h2: What happens at the Logan County tax sale?
sections.html:
The clerk advertises the open bills and offers them to outside buyers. For the 2025 bills, the clerk's page set the sale for Wednesday, July 29, 2026, at 10:00 am in the old courthouse courtroom. Half-page notices ran June 18, and the full list ran June 29.

Buyers sign up ahead. The clerk charges $5 per prior-year bill and $10 per current-year bill, capped at $250, takes a 25 percent deposit on current-year bills, and wants full payment on prior-year ones. A winning bidder steps into the lien, and the owner pays that buyer, who may add heavy fees. State rules call for a 30-day notice from the county attorney, a second notice within 60 days if needed, and a sale date that lands three to four and a half months after the bills reach the clerk.

If your house appears on the list, call the clerk before the date. Paying first keeps the lien out of an investor's hands.

sections.h2: How do I clear tax when selling a Logan County house?
sections.html:
Learn the balance before you sign anything, and let the closing agent show it on the settlement statement.

  • This year's balance comes from the Sheriff at 270-726-2244.
  • Older years sit with the County Clerk at 270-726-6061, with monthly interest and fees stacked on top.
  • For an inherited or vacant house, check whose name the tax roll shows before you list it.

Many local sellers are heirs, landlords or owners of older farmhouses. The faster you learn the exact payoff, the faster you can work out what you will net.

faqs.q: Where does a Logan County owner send the property tax payment?
faqs.a: To the Sheriff at 100 North Owen Street, Russellville, or through the link on the county's Sheriff page. Once April 15 passes, the bill shifts to the County Clerk at 229 West 3rd Street.

faqs.q: How big is the early-pay discount on a Logan County bill?
faqs.a: It is 2 percent, for payments made from October 1 through November 1. Face amount applies November 2 through year end, a 5 percent penalty starts in January, and 21 percent starts February 1.

faqs.q: Can I still dispute a Logan County assessment after the roll closes?
faqs.a: Yes. The dispute needs a PVA conference and a clerk filing by the workday after the inspection window ends. The window opens again in early May the following year.

faqs.q: Does the Logan County PVA set my tax rate or take payment?
faqs.a: Neither. The PVA's own page says it only assesses value and handles exemptions. Rates come from local taxing bodies, and the Sheriff takes payment.

faqs.q: What if a Logan County tax bill is already delinquent?
faqs.a: Call the County Clerk at 270-726-6061 for a payoff figure. The bill carries a lien, monthly interest and fees, and can be sold at the clerk's tax sale if it stays open.
